<x_0.0234><y_0.1352>" As to the rice fields, they differ in value, accor-
ding to the finenefs and quantity of rice they produce.
The growth of this grain has a particularity not un-
worthy of notice, viz. that as it loves a watery foil, fo
to whatever height the water rifes, wherever it is
planted, the growth of the rice keeps measure with it,
even to that of 12 and 14 feet; the fummit always ap-
pearing above the surface of the water. It is alfo re-
marked, that the eating of new rice affects the eyes.
The fact is certain, though the physical reason of it is
unknown.<x_0.7021><y_0.2852><class_Text>

<x_0.0225><y_0.2844>" Here and there are interfperfed fome few _brab_
trees, or rather wild palm trees (the word _brah_ being
derived from _brabs_, which in the Portuguese fignifies
wild.) They bear an infipid kind of fruit, about the
bignefs of a common pear; but the chief profit from
them is the toddy, or liquor drawn from them by in-
cifions at the top, of which the arrack is reckoned bet-
ter than that produced by the cocoa-nut trees. They
are generally near the fea-fide, as they delight moft in
a fandy foil. It is on this tree that the _toddy birds_, fo
called from their attachment to it, make their exqui-
litely curious nefts, wrought out of the thinneft reeds
and filaments of branches, with an inimitable mecha-
nifm. The birds themselves are about the fize of a
partridge, but are of no value either for plumage, fong,
or the table.<x_0.7012><y_0.5023><class_Text>

<x_0.0205><y_0.5016>" This illand is a strong influence of the benefits of
a good government, and a numerous population, by
not a fpot of it remaining uncultivated: fo that tho'
it is far from producing sufficient for the confumption
of its inhabitants, and notwithlanding its many difad-
vantages of situation and foil, it yields incomparably
more than the adjacent illand of Salfette."<x_0.6904><y_0.5984><class_Text>

<x_0.0186><y_0.5977>Among the curiosities of Bombay Mr Ives mentions
a large _terapin_ or land tortoife kept at the governor's
houfe, the age of which was upwards of 200 years.
Frogs, which abound every where through the Eaft
Indies, are very large at Bombay. Our author law
one that measured 22 inches from the extremities of
the fore and hind feet when extended; and he fuppo-
fes that its weight would not have been left than four
or five pounds. On the fea-thore round the illand are
a great variety of beautiful shells, particularly the fort
called _ventle-traps_ or _vendle-traps_, held in great e-
feem among the ladies fome time ago. Several pounds
Sterling are fold to have been given by a _virtuofs_ for
one of thefe hells when the Commodore Leflie’s col-
lection of hells was fold by auction.<x_0.6865><y_0.8016><class_Text>

<x_0.0166><y_0.8008>Mr Ives enumerates the following kinds of fnakes
found on this illand and other parts of the British em-
pire in the Eaft Indies. 1. The _cobra de capella_, grow-
ing from four to eight or nine feet long. They kill
by their bite in 15 minutes. 2. The _cobra manila_ is
a fmall bluith fnake, of the fize of a man's little finger,
and about a foot long, frequently teen about old walls.
